$comment: The launch registry. This list is the marketing: it has to make the
claim 'pair with literally anything' true on sight, which means the
credible half and the absurd half both have to be here and both have to
actually resolve.
`source` is what the relayer implements, not something the program
reads. Push-feed entries name a Pyth symbol rather than a feed id -
resolve the id at deploy time from Pyth's own registry instead of
pasting a hex string nobody can verify by eye.
`fulfillment` is only enabled where a unit is a thing an agent can
actually buy on demand. Everything else is quoted and settled, and the
UI must not imply otherwise.

`valuation` says how to read the index. 'price' means one unit is a real purchasable quantity and the index is its dollar price. 'scalar' means the thing has no price at all: one unit is the whole measurement and its current level is used directly as the dollar-equivalent index. A scalar pairing is a ratio, never a claim that one Phoenix degree costs $105, and the UI must render units and never dollars-per-unit for these.

`assetMint` is the tokenized version of the thing, and it is the whole of HARD grade: a market can hold it directly, so units are tokens, no price is consulted on any value-moving path, and coverage is 1.00 by construction. The program enforces that hard grade and a set assetMint imply each other.

Vetting rule, learned the hard way. Symbol: never - there are a dozen mints called SPYx and eleven of them are pump launches with $2k behind them. Liquidity alone: necessary but NOT sufficient - the deepest thing matching 'USDC' on Jupiter is jlUSDC, a yield-bearing wrapper, not USDC. So the mint address is the identity, it is curated and pinned here by hand, and liquidity is used to VERIFY a pinned address still has depth rather than to discover which address to use. `npm run verify-mints` re-checks these.

Depth is checked at a size, not as a number. A mint's liquidity figure and what it can actually fill disagree often enough to matter: BRK.Bx reports $27k of liquidity and still absorbs $25,000 at 1.53%, which a $27k pool could not do. So every hard entry records the price impact of a $25,000 buy and the date it was measured, because an undated depth claim goes stale silently. Repeated quotes on the same afternoon differ by a point or more on the thinner mints, since the route changes under you, which is why several entries record a range rather than a figure. No route at $25,000 but a route at $1,000 is thin; no route at either is dead. KOx is thin, SLVx is dead, and both are why their pairables stay INDEX.

`vaultable` is the criterion that decides whether an asset can back a permissionless market at all, and it is narrower than whether the asset is any good: defaultAccountState must not be frozen, and the transfer hook slot must be empty. A frozen default state means the vault's own ATA arrives frozen and nothing can be deposited until the issuer thaws it by hand; an installed hook means transfer_checked needs extra accounts the program does not pass. That rule, and not a policy about who we like, is why the tokenized treasuries are absent: BUIDL and BENJI enforce allowlists through a hook, USTB, USCC and USYC default new accounts to frozen, and OUSG is a dormant mint with no supply. Jupiter independently calls all six untradable. They could be INDEX pairables priced by an oracle with no custody; they can never be vault assets. `verify-mints` keeps re-checking them, because an issuer can change its mind.

`expiresAt` / `terminal` / `successor` describe a pairable's life. Almost everything here is perpetual (0), and that is the right default for a memecoin: you do not want your token's denominator to run out. Dated pairables are for things whose DEFINITION expires rather than whose feed goes quiet - a futures contract month, a crop year, a valuation 'as of' a tender. Expiry never breaks a market: pushes stop, the last TWAP becomes the final print, and accrual and claims carry on against it. `Roll` names a successor and `roll_market` redenominates value-neutrally; `Settle` means the final print stands forever. The crop-year pattern (PEAR-CY26 -> PEAR-CY27) is exercised in tests rather than seeded here, because shipping a pairable that expires in 2027 with a successor nobody maintains is a liability, not a feature.

A pairable must fix EVERY dimension that materially moves its number. For pears that meant one price tier (retail runs 2-3x wholesale). For a Big Mac it means one country, because Switzerland runs far above the US and India's Maharaja Mac far below. And `crossCheckOnly` sources fix a third dimension, cadence: a slow authoritative print bands the fast source rather than voting in its median.

`issuerPowers` is why HARD grade is NOT simply better than INDEX. Every xStock and PAXG is a Token-2022 mint carrying compliance extensions: permanentDelegate is a clawback, pausableConfig freezes transfers, defaultAccountState gates who may hold it at all. A vault holding SPYx has traded coverage risk for issuer risk - different risk, not less of it - and the UI has to say so. Read from chain by `npm run verify-mints`, listed here so the app can show it without a mainnet round-trip.

The same extensions also mean Meteora's DBC REFUSES these as pool quote mints: `is_supported_quote_mint` waves through any classic SPL mint but allows Token-2022 only when MetadataPointer and TokenMetadata are its sole extensions. So a Native market's POOL is quoted in USDC while its VAULT holds the asset, and the crank swaps between them. The program never tied those two together, which is the reason that works.

produce.$note: Fresh produce gaps hard at season turns - domestic pears run out around June and imports take over - and a 25% week-over-week move is ordinary rather than an attack. A breaker sized for a 15-second Pyth feed would trip on the harvest and freeze every market on it until governance intervened. The rule is to size the breaker to the largest plausible move BETWEEN PUSHES, which for a weekly series is enormous.

slowIndex.$note: For numbers that are authoritative and slow. A semi-annual print under an httpDaily window would go stale two days after every publication, permanently. The TWAP window is a day rather than an hour because smoothing a series that moves monthly at hourly resolution does nothing.

cheapSku.$note: The floor is the whole preset. A 20oz Coke is $2.49 and a parcel is $8 to $10, so a one-bottle request costs four times the bottle to honour and reads as the protocol being trolled rather than used. $25 is roughly a case, which is what these things actually ship as. The lesson came from pears and was not carried back here until someone walked the Coke case through.

produce.$note: A floor as well as a ceiling. Produce moves by the carton and shipping a single pear costs several times the pear, so a request under ~a carton is not worth quoting. The TTL matters more for perishables than for anything else: 'we will ship when they are back in season' is indistinguishable from never, so anyone may reclaim an unsettled request after a week.

voucher.$note: For things that cannot be posted. A Big Mac is a hot prepared item with a ten minute quality life and a gallon of petrol is not going in a parcel, so the deliverable is a claim on the good rather than the good: a gift card or fuel card worth N units. The floor is higher than a shipped SKU because a $6 voucher is not worth the transaction, and the TTL is shorter because a redeemable claim that nobody has actioned in two days is not coming.

pairables.name: A bottle of Coca-Cola
pairables.source: No live source is wired. The value is an operator attestation in relayer.yaml with the date it was true on it, and the gate gives it a two-day shelf life, so it holds rather than publishes once it ages. Walmart's item API, Target RedSky and the Kroger product API all want a key and a contract. The keyless near miss is BLS: APU0000FN1101 prices soft drinks per 2 litre bottle and APU0000FN1102 per 12 oz in a 12-pack, which prorate to $0.67 and $1.01 for 20 oz against a typed $2.49. Both are multiserve packaging and this is one chilled single, a tier that sells at 2.5x the 12-pack rate and 3.7x the 2 litre rate per ounce. Since `fulfillment` is cheapSku, somebody can settle this by handing over the bottle, so quoting the fridge-pack rate would misprice a settlement anyone can perform.

pairables.name: A dozen large eggs
pairables.source: BLS series APU0000708111, Average Price Data, US city average. One source, and the badge says one: the Walmart cross-check this entry used to claim was never wired, and the FRED binding that stood in for it was the same BLS series mirrored, which made the spread gate compare a number to itself. A real second opinion has to be a different survey of the same retail tier; USDA's egg reports are wholesale and pricing a retail dozen off them is a category error.

pairables.name: A gallon of whole milk
pairables.$fulfillmentNote: Milk needs a cold chain a fulfilment agent does not have, and a gallon that spent four days in a van is not the good that was quoted. A grocery card is.
pairables.source: BLS series APU0000709112, Average Price Data, US city average. One source. The grocery API cross-check this entry used to claim was never wired, and the FRED binding standing in for it read the same BLS series, so the second opinion was the first one restated.

pairables.name: A Big Mac in the US
pairables.source: No menu source is wired: McDonald's publishes no machine-readable US pricing. The value is an operator attestation carrying the Economist's own most recent Big Mac survey, the 2026-07-01 US row at $6.22, with the survey's date on it and a 200-day shelf life because the survey is semi-annual. The index is published as one CSV of the full history, oldest first, so the current row cannot be addressed from config at all: a match on the country name resolves to April 2000. The design note stands and is why this is an attestation rather than a feed - the Economist prints twice a year and menu pricing moves continuously, so the two could not be medianed even if both were wired, which is the same category error as medianing retail pears against wholesale. One jurisdiction per pairable: a Big Mac has no single price, so mixing US and Swiss quotes would be the geography version of mixing price tiers.

pairables.name: A Big Mac in Switzerland
pairables.source: No menu source is wired. The value is an operator attestation carrying the Economist's 2026-07-01 Swiss row, 7.30 CHF, quoted at the 0.80735 that survey used, so $9.04. The CHF leg is fixed at the survey's own rate rather than marked to today's, which keeps it one internally consistent July observation instead of two dates blended. Same 200-day shelf life and same addressing problem as BIGMAC-US: the index is one oldest-first CSV of the full history. Shipped alongside BIGMAC-US on purpose. The gap between them is purchasing-power parity, which is the joke and also the information.

pairables.name: A gallon of regular gasoline
pairables.$fulfillmentNote: A gallon of petrol cannot go in a parcel at any price: it is a hazmat shipment. The deliverable is a fuel card worth N gallons, which is what the voucher mode exists for.
pairables.source: EIA weekly US regular retail, AAA national average, GasBuddy

pairables.name: A pack of instant ramen
pairables.source: No live source is wired. The value is an operator attestation in relayer.yaml with the date it was true on it. Walmart and Target single-pack listings both want a key, and BLS has no instant noodle series at any tier: the nearest is spaghetti and macaroni per pound, which is dry pasta rather than a fried noodle block with a seasoning sachet and prorates 41% under the typed figure because it is a different product.

pairables.name: A 20lb bag of rice
pairables.source: BLS series APU0000701312, Average Price Data, US city average: rice, white, long grain, uncooked, dollars per POUND, monthly. Keyless. The pairable is a 20 POUND BAG, so the relayer multiplies by 20 and the config says so at the point of use. That conversion is arithmetic; the tier under it is not. BLS prices rice as households buy it, which is mostly 1 to 5 lb boxes, while a 20lb sack is the cheapest per pound there is, so this reads HIGH against a real bag by about the bulk discount: 22.00 in July 2026 against the 19.98 an operator had typed. One source, and the badge says one. The Walmart and Costco listings this entry used to name were never wired and both want a key and a contract, which is a procurement problem rather than a code one.

pairables.name: One pear
pairables.source: USDA AMS terminal markets, New York (NX_FV010) and Los Angeles (HC_FV010), medianed. The unit is a real one rather than an invented conversion: USDA quotes pears by carton AND by size count, so 'D'Anjou 80s at $48.00' means 80 pears in a 4/5 bushel carton and $0.60 a pear falls straight out of the published numbers. Retail (FVWRETAIL, weekly, per pound) is deliberately NOT medianed in - retail runs 2-3x wholesale FOB, so mixing tiers would read as a 200% provider disagreement and hold forever. One price tier per pairable. Both terminal-market bindings need an AMS Market News key (USDA_API_KEY); the api.data.gov key does not open it, so until that key exists the pairable runs on a single operator attestation and the badge reads short, which is the honest reading. There is no keyless substitute: BLS's Anjou pear series APU0000711413 still answers 200 and still returns a row, but the row has been the literal string "-" since 2025 M10 on the national series and on all four regional variants, which is worse than a dead endpoint because from the outside it looks alive.
pairables.$note: Seasonality is the feature. Cheaper pears mean your coin is worth MORE pears, so the September harvest collapses the denominator and every pear-denominated chart rips, then domestic supply exhausts in early summer and it gives back. A predictable annual cycle nobody has to manufacture.

pairables.name: Gold
pairables.source: Pyth Metal.XAU/USD. PAXG is one troy ounce of allocated gold, which is exactly this pairable's unit, a rare clean match between a tokenized asset and a real-world quantity. It stays pinned after a re-check on 2026-08-24: $25,000 routed at 0.21% impact against $518k of pool liquidity. The only other allocated-metal mint on Solana is Matrixdock's XAUm (5aLhp9VnUEKcsdtkfsf2DUgpJfomx7GmYVny24dHUZoB), also one troy ounce, and at 2.29% impact for the same order it is the fallback rather than the pin. Neither is GLDx, which is a share in a fund that holds gold and is filed as an equity for that reason. A third allocated-gold mint was verified on 2026-08-24 and is the cleanest of the three: Oro Finance GOLD (GoLDppdjB1vDTPSGxyMJFqdnj134yH6Prg9eqsGDiw6A), classic SPL with NO extensions at all and a freeze authority that is already REVOKED, so the issuer holds no power over a vault position whatsoever - which neither PAXG nor XAUm can say. It is one troy ounce, 9,936 holders, $321k of liquidity, and $23,000 sells at 0.00% impact with $113,000 at 1.23%. PAXG stays pinned only because it is deeper ($518k) and its unit is exactly this pairable's unit. Oro's yield is deliberately pushed into a SEPARATE staking action, so the base token never accrues inside a pool, which is the property this registry wants and the reason to switch the pin here the moment its depth passes PAXG's.

pairables.name: Silver
pairables.source: Pyth Metal.XAG/USD. Stays INDEX, and the reason has got worse rather than better since it was written: SLVx (XsxAd6okt8y1RRK6gNg7iJaqiWNiq5Md5EDf3ZrF2dm) is still there, but on 2026-08-24 Jupiter had no route for it at $25,000 or at $1,000, on $0.63 of pool liquidity. It is dead rather than thin. Silver has no PAXG: gold is hard grade because PAXG is one troy ounce of allocated metal with real depth behind it, and nothing on Solana does that for silver.

pairables.name: Copper
pairables.source: Pyth Metal.XCU/USD, converted to pounds

pairables.name: WTI crude
pairables.source: Pyth Commodities.WTI1M

pairables.name: Natural gas
pairables.source: FRED DHHNGSP, which is EIA's Henry Hub spot price, $/MMBtu. ONE source, and it needs FRED_API_KEY; without the key the pairable runs on an operator attestation carrying that series' own last published figure and date. This entry claimed two sources and a futures cross-check for months and had neither. The cross-check is not wired because there is nothing honest to wire: Pyth lists seven Henry Hub contracts and every one is unpublished at price 0 and publish_time 0, the same dead-feed condition that keeps Metal.XCU/USD out of COPPER-LB, and the keyless quote endpoints that do answer carry no parseable timestamp and quote the front-month future rather than spot, which prints the calendar spread as a price move on roll day.

pairables.name: One share of SPY
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.SPY/USD. Upgrades to HARD if an SPYx mint is used as the vault asset.

pairables.name: One share of NVIDIA
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.NVDA/USD

pairables.name: One share of Tesla
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.TSLA/USD

pairables.name: One share of Coca-Cola Co
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.KO/USD. Ships alongside COKE-20OZ deliberately: the stock and the bottle are different pairables and the difference is the joke. PROMOTED to hard grade on 2026-08-25. The note above said there was no liquid KOx; that is no longer true. KOx now carries $21,609, which clears the $20,000 floor, so the market can hold the real thing instead of only tracking it. Depth like this moves, and a claim about it is only as good as its date. Depth measured 2026-08-25 with a live quote rather than read off a liquidity field: $1,000 fills at 1.06%, and there is NO route at $25,000. This is a real market and a small one, and both halves matter. Size a launch against the figure that was measured, not against the reported liquidity.

pairables.name: One share of QQQ
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.QQQ/USD, cross-checked against the QQQx pool via Jupiter

pairables.name: One share of Apple
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.AAPL/USD, cross-checked against the AAPLx pool via Jupiter

pairables.name: One share of Microsoft
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.MSFT/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. $25,000 of USDC into MSFTx moved the price 2.09% on 2026-08-24, against $200k of pool liquidity. Comfortably vaultable, and thin enough that a market maker should size a fill rather than send it.

pairables.name: One share of Alphabet
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.GOOGL/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. $25,000 routed at 0.54% impact on 2026-08-24 against $243k of pool liquidity, which puts it in the top handful of xStocks by executable depth rather than by the liquidity figure, and the two do not always agree.

pairables.name: One share of Amazon
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.AMZN/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. $25,000 routed at 1.39% impact on 2026-08-24 against $172k of pool liquidity.

pairables.name: One share of Meta
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.META/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. $25,000 routed at 2.42% impact on 2026-08-24 against $44k of pool liquidity. One of the lowest liquidity figures on the list and the fill is still middling, which is the pattern across this whole set: quote the size you mean and believe the answer, not the pool number.

pairables.name: One share of Broadcom
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.AVGO/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. The thinnest entry that still clears the probe: $25,000 routed at 4.81% impact on 2026-08-24 through a single route, and it read the same on every re-measurement, against $50k of pool liquidity. Hard grade is still correct, because coverage comes from the vault holding the token and not from the fill, but this is the first one to demote if a later run cannot route $25,000 at all.

pairables.name: One share of Coinbase
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.COIN/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. $25,000 routed at 1.81% impact on 2026-08-24 against $762k of pool liquidity: worse depth than MSTRx while carrying a third more liquidity, which is why the impact number and not the liquidity number is the one recorded here.

pairables.name: One share of Robinhood
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.HOOD/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. $25,000 routed at between 2.14% and 3.72% impact across four measurements on 2026-08-24, against $150k of pool liquidity. That spread is the point of quoting rather than reading a liquidity figure: the route Jupiter picks changes through the day, and at the top of that band a $25,000 order is a bad fill rather than a trade.

pairables.name: One share of MicroStrategy
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.MSTR/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. $25,000 routed at between 0.57% and 0.89% impact across four measurements on 2026-08-24, against $579k of pool liquidity. The most reflexive pairable on the list: MSTRx is a levered claim on bitcoin wearing an equity ticker, so denominating a coin in it is a bet on that premium as much as on the bitcoin underneath.

pairables.name: One share of Circle
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.CRCL/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. The deepest xStock on the list by a distance: $25,000 moved the price between 0.04% and 0.27% across four measurements on 2026-08-24, against $2.8m of pool liquidity, which is what happens when the underlying is a crypto company and its holders are already on this chain. Circle also issues the dollar every market here quotes in, so a CRCL market is the registry pointed at its own plumbing.

pairables.name: One share of McDonald's
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.MCD/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. Ships alongside BIGMAC-US for the same reason KO ships alongside COKE-20OZ: the share and the sandwich are different pairables and the gap between them is the joke. $25,000 routed at between 1.90% and 2.30% impact across four measurements on 2026-08-24, against $48k of pool liquidity, so unlike KO this half of the pair is hard-quotable.

pairables.name: One share of Berkshire Hathaway B
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.BRK.B/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. This is the entry that taught the verifier to trust an executable quote over a liquidity field: Jupiter reports $27k of liquidity, which is under the registry's own floor, and yet $25,000 filled at between 1.03% and 1.53% impact across four measurements on 2026-08-24. A $27k pool cannot do that, so the quote is the ground truth and the floor is the smoke alarm.

pairables.name: One share of GLD
pairables.source: Pyth Equity.US.GLD/USD, cross-checked against the pool via Jupiter. Filed as an equity rather than a metal on purpose. GLDx tracks SPDR Gold Shares, the ETF, so a unit is a share in a fund that holds bullion and not the bullion itself: one derivative layer further from the metal than XAU-OZT, and it will drift from spot by the fund's fee. $25,000 moved it between 0.07% and 0.27% across four measurements on 2026-08-24, against $237k of pool liquidity.

pairables.name: One bitcoin
pairables.source: Pyth Crypto.BTC/USD

pairables.name: One ether
pairables.source: Pyth Crypto.ETH/USD

pairables.name: One SOL
pairables.source: Pyth Crypto.SOL/USD. HARD: the vault can hold wSOL, so coverage is pinned at 1.00. assetMint is the canonical wrapped-SOL mint, which reports its symbol as SOL rather than wSOL.

pairables.name: One Ethena USDe
pairables.source: The pool is the price, read through Jupiter. USDe is a synthetic dollar held near $1 by a delta-neutral hedge, spot crypto against short perpetuals, so it is neither a treasury claim nor a deposit and its peg depends on funding markets staying tradable. Filed under crypto rather than yield for exactly that reason. Classic SPL with no extensions and no freeze authority, so it hands its issuer no power over a vault's holdings at all, which is rarer among dollar tokens than it ought to be. $25,000 routed at 0.01% impact on 2026-08-24, against $8.8m of liquidity. Pinned by address after a supplied list handed over one mint labelled sUSDe that resolves to USDe and another labelled USDe that resolves to ENA, the governance token: the vetting rule at the top of this file is not theoretical.

pairables.name: One Ondo USDY
pairables.source: The pool is the price, read through Jupiter: no oracle publishes this and none needs to, because the vault holds the token itself. USDY is a claim on short-dated treasuries that accrues its yield into the token rather than paying it out, so one unit was worth $1.14 on 2026-08-24 and will be worth more tomorrow, which makes it a dollar that does not stand still. Classic SPL with no extensions at all, so nothing gates who may hold it, though the mint keeps a freeze authority that can freeze one account. $25,000 routed at 0.30% impact on 2026-08-24 against $2.9m of liquidity. No cooldown at all, and Ondo designed it as a freely transferable bearer asset that holders who never onboarded can still receive, so the KYC gate binds the primary market only. A 500,000 unit sell routed at 0.127% impact on 2026-08-24. Treasury-backed at 3.55%, which makes it the conservative half of the pair with syrupUSDC.

pairables.name: One Maple syrupUSDC
pairables.source: The pool is the price, read through Jupiter. syrupUSDC is a claim on a private credit book and not on treasuries: the yield comes from overcollateralised loans to trading firms, so it carries their credit rather than the government's, and the registry should not let the word yield blur those together. Deeper than any equity here and by a wide margin: $25,000 at 0.01% impact on 2026-08-24, against $11.7m of liquidity. Classic SPL with a freeze authority and no extensions. Redemption is a 24h notice into a FIFO queue that can run to 30 days, which is why the lock is recorded at its worst case rather than its typical one. It clears the gate on depth rather than on terms: a 500,000 unit sell into USDC routed at 0.027% impact on 2026-08-24, so a holder exits by selling and never touches the queue. That is the exact case the lock rule exists to distinguish - a cooldown is survivable only where the secondary market genuinely is.

pairables.name: One euro
pairables.source: Pyth FX.EUR/USD. Upgraded from an index perp to a real venue on 2026-08-24: EURC is Circle's euro, and at $711,561 across 55,735 holders it is the ONLY non-USD fiat stablecoin on Solana with a market rather than a listing - roughly equal to every other non-USD fiat stablecoin on the chain combined, and three times the next name. Classic SPL with no extensions at all, so it hands its issuer no power over a vault's holdings. The runners-up were checked and left as index perps: VCHF carries $240k across 760 holders and tGBP $236k across 80, both books a single LP could withdraw, and tGBP's issuer could not be identified at all. EURCV, which was expected here, turned out to be four abandoned impostor mints with revoked mint authorities and $21 of combined liquidity; Societe Generale has not deployed to Solana.

pairables.name: One hundred yen
pairables.source: Pyth FX.USD/JPY, inverted and scaled by 100 so the unit is legible

pairables.name: A month of NYC one-bedroom rent
pairables.source: No live source is wired. The value is an operator attestation in relayer.yaml with the date it was true on it. Zillow's ZORI metro file is keyless and carries New York at 3627.46 for July 2026, and is unusable two ways: it is a wide CSV whose current month can only be reached by naming the column, so after the next release the same path silently keeps returning the old month instead of failing, and ZORI is all-homes across the metro rather than a one-bedroom in the city, which is a different quantity rather than this one measured better. StreetEasy publishes no API.

pairables.name: The median US home
pairables.source: FRED MSPUS, median sales price of houses sold in the United States, quarterly. ONE source, and it needs FRED_API_KEY; without the key the pairable runs on an operator attestation carrying that series' own last published figure (410700, Q2 2026) with the quarter's date on it. The Zillow ZHVI cross-check this entry used to claim was never wired: Zillow publishes it as a wide CSV, one row per region and one column per month, and the current month can only be reached by naming it, which means the path keeps resolving to a stale column after the next release instead of failing.

pairables.name: A year of Ivy League tuition
pairables.source: Bonded assertion against published sticker tuition, mean of the eight schools. Annual, so the dispute window can be generous. Typed by design rather than pending a feed: `resolver` is optimistic, so the assertion IS the mechanism and a challenger takes the bond. IPEDS and College Scorecard both want an api.data.gov key and both lag the current academic year.

pairables.name: A month of Netflix standard
pairables.source: No live source is wired. The value is an operator attestation in relayer.yaml with the date it was true on it. Netflix has no pricing API and the plans page is JS-rendered and varies by geography: fetched from here it returns four prices, none of which is the US standard tier, which is the argument against scraping it rather than for.

pairables.name: An hour of US federal minimum wage
pairables.source: Pinned at $7.25 until Congress does something. The most honest pinned constant on the list.

pairables.name: Drake's monthly listeners
pairables.source: No live source is wired. The value is an operator attestation in relayer.yaml with the date it was true on it. Spotify's own API needs OAuth, and the keyless counters that mirror YouTube for MRBEAST-SUBS expose FOLLOWERS rather than monthly listeners: 115,805,555 for Drake, a cumulative monotonic count where this pairable is a rolling 28-day one that falls as well as rises. pairables.name: One share of SpaceX
pairables.source: The pool is the price, read through Jupiter. Nothing publishes a feed for a private company, which is why this ran as an optimistic scalar on a hand-typed $350bn valuation until SPCXx gave it a token to hold. Upgrading it to HARD changes the unit as well as the grade: one unit was the whole company and is now one tokenized share, so the manual $350bn attestation and the 1e9 sanity floor in the relayer config both have to be replaced or this pairable holds instead of pushing, which is the safe direction to fail. THREE things, not two: app/public/data/history/SPACEX-VAL.jsonl kept thirteen whole-company rows in front of the per-share ones, and changeOver reads last over first across whatever is in the file, so the chart read -100% and spanned 2.6 billion times its real range until those rows were dropped. A regrade that changes the unit invalidates the old rows as a series; truncate the history at the first print in the new unit. $25,000 routed at between 0.12% and 0.91% impact across four measurements on 2026-08-24, against $1.18m of liquidity, deeper than most of the listed equities here.

pairables.name: One Etherfuse CETES
pairables.source: The pool is the price, read through Jupiter. A tokenised Mexican Cetes sovereign bill, denominated in pesos, and the single thing in this registry nobody else lists. 4,099 holders. $1,000 buys at about 0.10% impact and sells at 0.03% on Orca. Etherfuse issues it as a Token-2022 mint carrying exactly two extensions, interestBearingConfig and metadataPointer, and - unusually for a regulated instrument - NO freeze authority, no permanent delegate and no transfer hook. Etherfuse therefore cannot freeze or claw back a vault position even if it wanted to, which is a stronger custody position than any tokenised equity in this registry and stronger than XAUm. KYC lives at the fiat on and off ramp; the token itself is unrestricted. Two independent verification passes on 2026-08-24 resolved this mint byte for byte and agreed on its extension set. Yield arrives through the interest extension, so the raw amount a pool holds is stable while the displayed balance grows: reserves stay true and the UI must never quote the raw reserve as a balance. Quoted rate around 5.54% annualised. The fund behind it holds about $5.2m of Cetes across five chains, but only about $539,000 of that is ON SOLANA, roughly 10%; the bulk sits on Stellar. Solana supply against Solana pool depth is about five to one, which is the healthiest ratio in the family and the reason this is the one Etherfuse bond that behaves like a retail market. Depth measured 2026-08-25 with a live quote rather than read off a liquidity field: $1,000 fills at 0.11%, and there is NO route at $25,000. This is a real market and a small one, and both halves matter. Size a launch against the figure that was measured, not against the reported liquidity.

Listed on that basis, meaning the venue is the buy side until it deepens. Etherfuse issues it as a Token-2022 mint carrying exactly two extensions, interestBearingConfig and metadataPointer, and - unusually for a regulated instrument - NO freeze authority, no permanent delegate and no transfer hook. Etherfuse therefore cannot freeze or claw back a vault position even if it wanted to, which is a stronger custody position than any tokenised equity in this registry and stronger than XAUm. Quoted rate around 12.64% annualised. About $78,000 of it is on Solana out of $803,000 across chains. Pool depth exceeds Solana supply, which is possible only because the book is one-sided. pairables.name: One Hastra PRIME
pairables.source: The pool is the price, read through Jupiter. A claim on a pool of Figure-originated residential home-equity loans, and at $6,915,972 the DEEPEST vaultable real-world asset found anywhere on Solana - more liquidity on its own than the entire tokenised commodity and treasury set combined. Classic SPL Token, so a transfer hook and a frozen default account state are structurally impossible rather than merely absent; the freeze authority is set, so individual accounts can still be frozen after the fact. It marks above a dollar, which is the observable evidence that the yield accrues into the exchange rate rather than into the balance. This is credit risk, not sovereign risk, and the UI has to say which. 1,647 holders on 2026-08-24.

pairables.name: One OnRe ONYC
pairables.source: The pool is the price, read through Jupiter. A claim on tokenised reinsurance, which is a category this registry had not looked for and which correlates with almost nothing else in it: reinsurance pays out on catastrophe losses, not on rates or earnings. $5,527,968 of liquidity across 8,006 holders on 2026-08-24. Classic SPL Token, so no hook and no frozen default are possible. Marks above a dollar, so the premium income accrues into the exchange rate rather than the balance. Confirmed independently on 2026-08-24 as the LARGEST Solana-native staked dollar at roughly $275m of float, and the deepest: $250,000 routes at 0.02% in both directions and $1m sells at 0.20%. Classic SPL with zero extensions and a raw-to-UI multiplier of exactly 1.000000. Redemption is effectively shut to ordinary holders - capped at 2.5% of NAV a month, a 0.25% fee, accredited-only, US excluded - which is recorded as a primary-market gate rather than a cooldown because it delays nobody: transfers are unrestricted and the exit is the pool. The real risk to disclose is the live freeze authority 45Ynzauhs...W9H3jaJ5, which ONyc retains and eUSX does not.

pairables.name: One Huma PST
pairables.source: The pool is the price, read through Jupiter. The senior tranche of Huma's PayFi pool, a claim on payments receivables rather than on a security. $4,459,503 across 4,289 holders on 2026-08-24. Classic SPL Token with NO freeze authority at all, so the issuer holds no power over a vault's position whatsoever. Marks above a dollar, so yield accrues into the exchange rate. Senior means first in line on the waterfall, which is a real distinction from the leveraged mPST tranche and one the UI must not blur.

pairables.name: One Solstice eUSX
pairables.source: The pool is the price, read through Jupiter. The cleanest dollar-denominated mint found in the whole survey and the one to build the reference integration against: classic SPL Token, ZERO extensions of any kind, and a freeze authority that is not merely unused but DISABLED, so Solstice holds no power over a vault position at all. Verified directly on 2026-08-24: raw-to-UI multiplier exactly 1.000000, so there is no displayed-versus-held divergence to reason about anywhere. $8.2m of liquidity across 7,645 holders, and it marks at $1.0426, which is the observable evidence that rewards accrue into the exchange rate rather than into the balance. The 7-day cooldown (24 hours under $1,000) governs REDEMPTION only; Solstice's own documentation tells holders to swap out on a DEX instead, and $250,000 routes at 0.27% with $1m at 0.37%, so the exit that matters is open. Delta-neutral strategy, which is where the yield comes from and also where the risk does.

pairables.name: One share of Micron
pairables.source: The pool is the price, read through Jupiter. Micron Technology, tokenised by Backpack Securities, which decorates the MINT ADDRESS rather than the ticker: the symbol is the plain exchange symbol and the vanity lives in the address. That is why this registry resolves an underlying per issuer instead of stripping a suffix, and it is the reason a third issuer does not quietly break the deduplication. Verified on chain 2026-08-25: Token-2022, 6dp, vaultable (new accounts are not frozen by default and no transfer hook is installed), $1,476,341 of pool liquidity. Carries scaledUiAmountConfig, which is the sharpest edge here for an AMM: it is the stock-split mechanism, and when the issuer changes the multiplier the RAW amounts a pool holds do not move while the displayed balances all rescale. Reserves stay correct; anything that reads a UI amount does not. The transfer hook slot is present but empty, and its authority can fill it later, so vaultable here is a point-in-time verdict rather than a permanent property. Re-check before every launch batch.
